title: Stuck, Then Slipping: Friction and the Limit Cycle

questions.question: A joint with static friction is held by a proportional controller alone and stops short of its target. Why does it not close the last bit?
options: Friction is random
The sensor is wrong
The gain is too low to ever matter
The force stops growing once the error is small, and below the breakaway force the mass stays stuck, so it rests anywhere inside the band the breakaway over the gain allows
questions.explanation: With a breakaway of 1.5 N and a gain of 20 the band is 0.075, and it stopped at 0.0623.

questions.question: Why does adding an integral make the same joint hunt?
options: It keeps pushing until the force passes the breakaway, the mass lets go with more force than it needs, overshoots, sticks on the far side, and the integral winds the other way
The sampling rate is too low
The integral is unstable on its own
The integral adds noise
questions.explanation: A limit cycle between the controller and the friction. A gain of 5 settled and 20 and 50 hunted, by more the bigger the gain.

questions.question: A force of 1.2 N will not start a mass whose breakaway is 1.5 N. What does it do to the same mass once it is moving?
options: Reverses it
Stops it at once
Accelerates it for ever
Keeps it going, because the force that keeps a mass moving, the Coulomb force of 1.0 N, is less than the force that started it, and it settles at 0.4 m/s
questions.explanation: Stiction is larger than Coulomb friction, so a range of forces keeps a mass going and will not start it.

questions.question: Why is friction modelled as a stuck or slipping state and not as sign(velocity) times a force?
options: It uses less memory
The sign function is not defined
At exactly zero velocity the sign form gives no force, and a mass crossing zero in discrete time chatters from one side to the other and never stops
A state is faster
questions.explanation: The state form stops the mass when a step would carry it through zero, and then holds it exactly still.

questions.question: Freezing the integral inside a band of 0.01 stopped the hunting with a final error of 0.0051, and a band of 0.08 left it 0.0367 off. What is the lesson?
options: A band trades the hunting for a steady error about as large as the band, so it should be as narrow as the joint can resolve and no wider than the error you can tolerate
Always use the widest band
Bands do not work
The error does not depend on the band
questions.explanation: A wide band is quiet and wrong by more than the oscillation ever was.

questions.question: A loop has a steady error of 0.5 that never changes. Does analyze_hunting report hunting?
options: It cannot say
No: hunting needs a swing and crossings of the signal's own mean, and a large steady offset has neither
Yes, the error is large
Yes, because it never settles to zero
questions.explanation: Crossings are counted about the mean, not zero, so a loop that hunts about an offset is still hunting, and one sitting steadily off zero is not.
